Variants.Content: The Giant's Lance towers over the Vale, with the Eyrie built near its summit and the Gates of the Moon guarding the approach at its foot. The steep path to the Eyrie passes in turn through Stone, Snow, and Sky, growing ever less suited to wagons and formed bodies of troops the higher it climbs; the final stretch relies on winch baskets or narrow mountain tracks to haul men and supplies. Height makes the Eyrie nearly impossible to storm, yet imposes severe limits: winter snows, rockfalls, and lack of farmland cut off supplies, forcing the household to descend to the Gates of the Moon in the cold season. The safety of the Giant's Lance comes from distance and hardship, and its price is distance and hardship alike.

Knights of the Vale take pride in the steepness of the Giant's Lance, yet know that long defense truly rests on the storehouses at the mountain's foot and each of the waycastles. An enemy may not be able to fight its way up, yet hunger needs no scaling ladders.

Mountain folk, muleteers, and masons do not look upon the Eyrie merely as a wonder. They remember how every sack of grain goes up the mountain and how every block of stone was hauled, knowing that the safety of highborn lords is held aloft by countless frost-cracked hands.
Outsiders gazing up at the peak easily believe it can never fall. Those who understand history and supply add a further word: impregnable and habitable are not the same thing.
